title: Greenfield Rust parsing library: parse_int, parse_csv_row, parse_key_value
description: Start from an empty Rust module and implement three simple text-parsing functions with tests.

task_spec.prompt:
Create src/lib.rs in this Rust project with three parsing functions:

1. pub fn parse_int(s: &str) -> Result<i64, String>
   Parses s as a base-10 integer. Returns Ok(n) on success, Err(msg) on failure.
   Examples: parse_int("42") == Ok(42), parse_int("-7") == Ok(-7), parse_int("abc") == Err(...).

2. pub fn parse_csv_row(s: &str) -> Vec<String>
   Splits s on commas and returns each field trimmed of whitespace. Empty string returns vec![""]. 
   Examples: parse_csv_row("a, b, c") == ["a", "b", "c"], parse_csv_row("") == [""].

3. pub fn parse_key_value(s: &str) -> Option<(String, String)>
   Expects the format KEY=VALUE (first '=' splits key and value). Returns None if no '=' present.
   Examples: parse_key_value("name=Alice") == Some(("name", "Alice")), parse_key_value("url=http://x=y") == Some(("url", "http://x=y")), parse_key_value("noequals") == None.

Write 2 tests per function (6 total). cargo test must show 6 tests passing. cargo build must succeed.
success_criteria: parse_csv_row splits on commas and trims whitespace
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `cargo test` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
